items.title: Defensive SEO: How to protect your brand narrative in AI search
items.summary: Defensive SEO focuses on shaping brand perception in AI-powered search by monitoring and influencing how AI tools summarize brands, especially for evaluation queries like “Is [BRAND] worth it?” It involves proactive narrative management through AI visibility audits, updating source material, and addressing evaluation content to reduce ambiguity and reinforce accurate positioning. This shift addresses AI's compression of complex stories, reliance on third-party signals, and amplification of existing narratives, making narrative ownership essential in the new search landscape.

items.title: AI citation data shows there is no universal top source for brands
items.summary: AI citation patterns vary significantly by platform, industry, and intent, with no single top source like Reddit applying universally—Reddit grew 73% in citations overall but showed dramatic differences across categories and platforms. Google's AI surfaces, including AI Overviews, Gemini, and AI Mode, cite social media and web sources differently, with divergences like Reddit at 44% for AI Overviews versus 5% for Gemini. This emphasizes the need for category-specific strategies in AI search amid shifts like Amazon blocking AI crawlers.

items.title: Organic search is fundamentally disrupted. Here's what to do about it.
items.summary: Organic search is disrupted by rising AI Overviews and LLM usage, leading to zero-click searches (over 65%) and traffic declines, with content often cited without clicks. To adapt, focus on AEO by optimizing for citations through E-E-A-T, structured content with Q&A formats, human-written quality over AI-generated volume, recency, and objective language, while building external mentions. Measure success with metrics like citations, brand mentions, share of voice, sentiment, and AI-influenced traffic.

items.title: AIO Citations Diverge From Rankings, Bing Rewrites Rules – SEO Pulse
items.summary: AI Overview citations from top-ranking pages dropped from 76% to 38% overlap with Google's top 10, as AI Overviews trigger on 48% of searches with YouTube most cited. Bing updated guidelines with NOARCHIVE for AI control and expanded abuse definitions, while Google removed outdated JS advice. Optimize for AI visibility beyond traditional rankings.

items.title: 3 AI Search Changes Every Marketer Needs A Plan For In Q2
items.summary: AI search shifts from visibility to measurement and budgeting, with ads appearing in AI answers impacting discovery, clicks, and conversions. Q1 data highlights changes across platforms, urging plans for KPIs and strategy from Forrester research. Free event covers AI search implications for marketers.

items.title: Self-publish and be scammed: Jon’s tale of heartbreak highlights boom in fraudsters using AI to supercharge book swindles
items.summary: The article details how AI has fueled a surge in publishing scams targeting self-published authors, with fraudsters using automated tools to send personalized solicitations promising bestseller status, marketing, and film deals in exchange for upfront fees. Jon Cocks, a self-published author, lost nearly A$10,000 to such schemes involving fake book trailers, reviews, and nonexistent publishing services. These operations, often based in south Asia, the Philippines, and Nigeria, mimic romance scams and exploit the growing number of self-published books.

items.title: Amazon pulls sponsorship from Paris book festival after booksellers’ association boycott
items.summary: Amazon has withdrawn its sponsorship from the Paris book festival, set for 17-19 April, following a boycott by France’s Syndicat de la Librairie Française (SLF) over the company’s involvement. The SLF accused Amazon of attempting to flood the market with fake AI-generated books promoted by fake reviews and rankings. Organisers ended the partnership to avoid disruption and ensure a peaceful event.

items.title: UK Society of Authors launches logo to identify books written by humans not AI
items.summary: The UK Society of Authors has introduced a registration scheme allowing authors to certify their books as human-authored and display a 'Human Authored' logo on covers, addressing the challenge of distinguishing human-written works from AI-generated ones in a flooded market. This initiative, launched by Tracy Chevalier at the London Book Fair, mirrors a similar US program by the Authors Guild and responds to the lack of government mandates for AI content labeling. It emphasizes protecting authors' creativity amid concerns over AI trained on copyrighted material without compensation.

items.title: Official BookTok chart set to launch in the UK
items.summary: An official BookTok chart is set to launch in the UK later this year, providing a monthly Top 20 ranking that combines retail sales data with TikTok social media engagement to identify popular titles. The chart will be compiled by NielsenIQ BookData in partnership with Media Control, using an algorithm weighted towards sales volume. BookTok has become a key driver in publishing, boosting sales of genres like romance, fantasy, and romantasy.

items.title: AWP 2026 Takes On AI
items.summary: The Association of Writers & Writing Programs (AWP) Conference and Bookfair in Baltimore from March 4–7, 2026, featured multiple panels addressing the impacts of generative AI on literature and publishing, emphasizing that writing remains a human expression and that AI lacks the ability to generate meaning, truth, or nuance. Panelists discussed AI's practical uses for tasks like manuscript organization while cautioning against its use in writing due to ethical concerns such as training on stolen books and its carbon footprint. The event underscored a strong demand for human connection in publishing amid AI discussions.

items.title: I asked Kat Rosenfield about her new book and The Free Press | Opinion
items.summary: Kat Rosenfield, a novelist and culture writer at The Free Press cofounded by Bari Weiss, discusses her new thriller novel 'How to Survive in the Woods' and how her fiction and nonfiction writing intersect in exploring cultural questions like fairness and loyalty. She reflects on her freelance role at The Free Press, emphasizing its role in addressing gaps in the media landscape, and promotes her book tour drawing from her prior experience as a publicist in publishing. Rosenfield critiques the erosion of political labels into tribal signifiers, advocating for skepticism to maintain shared truth in storytelling.

items.title: Disney Star Rachel Zegler Refuses to 'Assimilate' After 'Snow White' Backlash
items.summary: Rachel Zegler responded to backlash over her casting in Disney's live-action Snow White remake and her controversial posts by stating she refuses to assimilate for others' comfort and has faced threats to her safety. The film, released in 2025, reportedly lost Disney about $170 million at the box office amid criticism labeled as 'woke.' She emphasized her commitment to her beliefs in a Harper’s Bazaar UK interview published March 10, 2026.

items.title: Woke ‘The Bride!’ Bombs at Box Office, Crushed by Disney's ‘Hoppers’
items.summary: 'The Bride!' earned $7.26 million in its opening weekend across 3,304 theaters on March 9, 2026, falling short of $16-18 million projections. Disney/Pixar's 'Hoppers' grossed $46 million in its opening weekend, while 'Scream 7' earned $17.3 million in its second weekend. The underperformance is attributed to audience preferences amid industry trends.

items.title: Scary Movie 6 Trailer Sparks Backlash Over Pronoun Joke
items.summary: The Scary Movie 6 trailer released on March 2, 2026, features a joke where a bleeding character corrects 'My pronouns are they/them. He stabbed 'them'!,' prompting online backlash from some viewers labeling it transphobic. Others defend it as classic parody humor in line with the franchise's style. The controversy highlights divided reactions to gender-related content.

items.title: 'Sinners' Wins Top Prize at 2026 Actor Awards
items.summary: 'Sinners,' a vampire film set in the segregated South directed by Ryan Coogler, won the top ensemble prize at the 2026 Actor Awards on March 1, 2026. Michael B. Jordan received Best Male Actor for his dual role. The film triumphed over Oscar nominees like 'One Battle After Another.'

items.title: Pixar's 'Hoppers' Leads March 2026 Box Office with Strong Opening
items.summary: Pixar's 'Hoppers' grossed $46 million in its opening weekend as of March 9, 2026, topping charts amid new releases. The film is highlighted alongside other March titles like Ryan Gosling's 'Project Hail Mary' and 'Youngblood.' It outperforms competitors in a busy release month.

items.title: AI Readiness Report: SMB AI Optimism Outpaces Adoption
items.summary: SMB leaders exhibit strong optimism toward AI, with over 70 percent holding positive views, but adoption and maturity remain uneven due to gaps in skills and data readiness. AI is primarily focused on data analysis, reporting, content creation, marketing, customer service, and inventory management, yet nearly 40 percent report no measurable results from initiatives. Labor shortages and operational challenges in manufacturing, distribution, and field service industries are accelerating AI urgency, though barriers like lack of in-house expertise and data issues hinder impact on small businesses.

items.title: AI adoption for small business marketing ops continues
items.summary: In a challenging economic environment, small- and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) are leveraging artificial intelligence to get a leg up when it comes to marketing operations. More than half (54%) of SMB owners are already using AI marketing tools, according to a new survey from digital marketing tools provider Constant Contact, with nearly half (45%) using AI to analyze trend data and 44% to compose content. Three-quarters (74%) of SMBs surveyed expect to spend more time on marketing this year, and more than two-thirds (68%) plan to increase marketing budgets.

items.title: Small Business in the Age of AI: Tools, Tactics and Practical Wins
items.summary: Small businesses adopting AI report saving $500-$2,000 monthly and reclaiming over 20 hours, with 68% of U.S. small businesses now using AI regularly, up from 48% a year ago. Key tools include ChatGPT Plus for content creation and planning at $20/month, Canva Pro for design at $15/month, HubSpot for CRM and automation starting free with paid plans from $45/month, and Notion AI for project management at $10/month per user. AI delivers immediate impact in content marketing by saving 1.2 hours daily per team member, customer service with 80% automation and cost reductions, and personalization that boosts conversion rates up to 30%.

items.title: Small Service Businesses Turn to Custom AI Systems to Streamline Operations and Reduce Manual Work
items.summary: Small and mid-size service businesses, including law firms and transportation companies, are increasingly adopting custom AI systems from firms like Speed Wraith to address industry-specific operational bottlenecks rather than using broad off-the-shelf software. Speed Wraith builds platform-agnostic AI integrations that work with existing tools, as demonstrated in cases where a transportation company automated contracts and proposals to boost closed deals, and a personal injury law firm doubled intake volume with an AI-powered screening system. Co-founder Kenneth Chiba emphasizes that their approach makes AI easy by tailoring solutions to each business's unique workflows and tools.

items.title: Launch Commerce Rebrands from Launch Cart, Unveils AI-Powered Business Platform for Small Businesses
items.summary: Launch Commerce, Inc., formerly Launch Cart, Inc., announced its rebrand and rollout of an AI-powered business platform with seven integrated products for small and mid-sized companies to automate operations, capture leads, and drive revenue. The ecosystem includes Launch AI Workforce for AI receptionist and automation, Launch CRM for customer management, Launch Ads for advertising, Launch Webinars for webinars, Launch Cart for e-commerce, Launch Data for intent-based intelligence, and Launch AI Academy for training. Founded in 2019 in Carlsbad, CA, the company targets service businesses like HVAC and law firms, with the name change effective December 2025.
